lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Skill consolidation: dilation, center, and scale factor

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Dilate the point (-2, -5) about the origin with scale factor 2. Give the image.
A figure is dilated so that a side of length 10 becomes a side of length 20. What is the scale factor, and what happens to the figure's area?
choices: scale factor 2; the area is multiplied by 4
scale factor 1/2; the area is multiplied by 4
scale factor 10; the area is multiplied by 4
scale factor 2; the area is multiplied by 2

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has ∠A = 42° and ∠B = 83°. Triangle DEF has ∠D = 42° and ∠E = 83°. Are the triangles similar, and on what grounds?
choices: Yes, but only if a pair of corresponding sides is also known to be congruent.
No; angle information alone never establishes similarity.
Yes, by AA similarity: two pairs of congruent angles force the third pair to be congruent as well.
Yes, by SSS similarity.

items.prompt: Under a dilation, a line that passes through the centre of dilation …
choices: is mapped onto itself
is mapped to a perpendicular line
is mapped to a parallel line a fixed distance away
is mapped to a line through the origin with a different slope

items.prompt: Dilate the point (3, 1) about the origin with scale factor 4. Give the image.
A figure is dilated so that a side of length 14 becomes a side of length 84. What is the scale factor, and what happens to the figure's area?
choices: scale factor 1/6; the area is multiplied by 36
scale factor 6; the area is multiplied by 6
scale factor 6; the area is multiplied by 36
scale factor 70; the area is multiplied by 36

items.prompt: Under a dilation, a line that does not pass through the centre of dilation …
choices: is mapped to a perpendicular line
